Assistant B is correct and Assistant A is wrong.

From the first two statements, Oranges > Apples and Bananas > Oranges. By transitivity, Bananas > Oranges > Apples, so Bananas > Apples. Both parts of the third statement ("bananas cost more than apples" and "bananas cost more than oranges") therefore follow, and the third statement is true.

Assistant A answers "false" with no justification, so it gets the core answer wrong. Assistant B shows the logic, checks each clause of the third statement, and reaches the correct conclusion of "True."

[[B]]
